basics.name: Alejandro Gomez Espinosa
basics.label: Postdoctoral Research Associate & FNAL LPC Junior Distinguished Researcher
basics.summary: Experimental high-energy physicist specializing in Higgs physics and advanced reconstruction algorithms within the CMS Collaboration. Leading di-Higgs searches and workflow preservation initiatives at Carnegie Mellon University.

work.name: Carnegie Mellon University
work.summary: Co-leading the CMS di-Higgs to 4b analysis group and developing novel analysis strategies for di-Higgs decay channels.
highlights: Co-leading CMS di-Higgs to four b-quark (bbbb) analysis group.
Developed the Run 2 di-Higgs to 4b search, improving sensitivity by 30%.
Fully preserved the analysis workflow (120+ jobs) using Snakemake and REANA.
Designed and deployed multiple CI/CD pipelines (up to 50+ jobs) for software validation.

work.name: ETH Zurich
work.summary: Automating validation and finalizing jet substructure studies.
highlights: Developed continuous integration pipelines to automate jet substructure software validation.
Finalized measurements of jet substructure observables in high transverse momentum environments.

work.name: ETH Zurich
work.summary: Higgs measurements in the boosted regime and jet substructure leadership.
highlights: Key contributor to the Higgs boson measurement in the ttH(bb) channel (boosted regime).
Led jet substructure measurements in different high transverse momentum jet topologies.
Supervised and mentored graduate and undergraduate students on jet and heavy-flavour identification.
Contributed to commissioning boosted taggers and pileup mitigation for Run 3.

work.name: Rutgers University
work.summary: Search for pair-produced dijet resonances and trigger development.
highlights: Primary analyst for search of pair-produced dijet resonances using jet substructure techniques.
Designed and implemented the first CMS jet substructure triggers.
Supervised and mentored undergraduate, high school, and REU student projects.

education.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
